summary: The L-shaped southwestern portion of Block 7 at Humboldt St and Louisiana Paseo, approved March 2, 2022 for a Foster + Partners-designed 27-story, approximately 237-ft market-rate tower with 325 units, ground-floor retail and childcare over a basement garage; the tallest building permitted on the site. No building permit or construction start has been reported as of September 2026. The developer's amended and restated development agreement, which includes Housing, Transportation and Phasing Plan amendments, passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (legislative event date; enactment is not confirmed).

milestones.text: Phase 1 Development Phase Application approved: Block 7 to include approximately 345 market-rate units plus a 100% affordable building; Phase 1 includes Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 15
Design review pre-application community meeting for Blocks 7 and 8
Design Review Application for Block 7A submitted (Case 2017-011878PHA-04); the Planning Department's staff memo gives December 19, 2020, while the developer's 2021 annual report table prints 12.18.20
Planning filings published by SF YIMBY describe Block 7A as a 240-ft, 25-story tower with 277 apartments (Foster + Partners)
Site-wide groundbreaking; Foster + Partners releases updated renderings describing Block 7A as 240 ft with 277 units

Planning Commission informational hearing on Block 7A (required for buildings 200 ft or taller); Commission 'commended the project team'; SF YIMBY's preview (Jul 14, 2021) describes a 27-story tower with 325 apartments (the hearing slides show no story count or 7A-only unit count; their 'Current Phase 1' slide shows Block 7 (7A with 7b) at 420 units)

Planning Director approves the Block 7A design review with three minor modifications (D4D 6.5.1 floorplate 13,077 sq ft vs 12,000; 6.5.2 diagonal 166 ft 5 in vs 160 ft at levels 9-10; 6.5.4 tower separation 107 ft 4 in vs 115 ft from Block 15)
2024 DA compliance report: 'Developer has submitted no building permits for any market-rate housing projects'; Block 7A still described as approximately 325 market-rate units
Ordinance for an Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) introduced, including Housing Plan, Transportation Plan and Phasing Plan amendments

Planning Commission recommends the DA amendments 6-0; residential height limits to rise by up to 8 ft, so the tallest residential tower could reach 248 ft (the Chronicle does not name the block; the Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary says the maximum height 'would increase from 240 feet to 248 feet on Block 7' and lists Block 5's existing maximum as 220 feet, so the 240-ft limit is Block 7's, although the D4D's Standard 6.2.2 puts both blocks in the 181-240 ft highrise class)
Board of Supervisors hearing on the Amended and Restated DA noticed (Land Use and Transportation Committee)

Board of Supervisors passes the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770) on first reading; Legistar's history lists '9/29/2026 ... Board of Supervisors ... PASSED, ON FIRST READING ... Pass' for both. The Mayor's approval and enactment on October 13, 2026 are the next milestone. All dates here are legislative event dates as listed by the Clerk of the Board (first-reading row read October 12 and again October 14, 2026)

Mayor approves the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): Legistar lists both as 'Status: Passed' with 'Final action: 10/13/2026', 'Enactment date: 10/13/2026' and enactment numbers 208-26 (File 260724) and 209-26 (File 260770), and a history row '10/13/2026 ... Mayor ... APPROVED' for each. The Board of Supervisors' own 10/6/2026 history row still shows no action or result ('Not available'), so no Board vote on that date is shown. The date is the enactment date, from the Clerk of the Board's listing (page read October 14, 2026); it is an event date, not a Board vote result.

details.text: Height of Block 7A: the plan set gives 237 ft 3 in to the uppermost structural slab; the 264 ft to the top of the screened mechanical level is 240 ft plus 10% for non-occupied features. Earlier press gave 240 ft (March 2021).

Use of Block 7A: the design review approval shows a childcare facility of approximately 6,270 sq ft; SocketSite (July 2021) said 6,000 sq ft. The development agreement's Phasing Plan requires childcare facilities for the project as a whole, so the requirement is not tied to Block 7A. The 2024 annual compliance report says the developer 'currently anticipates that all 778 units proposed as part of Phase 1 would be rental units' (an anticipation, and the units would also be mapped as condominiums; the design review approval does not say rental).

open_questions: Construction start: none found. Searched the 2021-2024 DA compliance reports (the 2024 report says no market-rate building permits have been submitted), SF YIMBY through Sept 2026, the Chronicle (Jul 29 and Aug 3, 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025) and Potrero View (Oct 2025). SocketSite (Jul 2021) said construction was 'slated to commence in 2023'; SF YIMBY (Mar 2021) said Block 7 construction was expected to start 'by 2023, with completion by 2026'. Neither happened.

The July 2026 Chronicle line 'tallest residential tower would be permitted to reach 248 feet' does not name a block. The Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary (Resolution No. 21945, attached to BOS File 260724) says the amendment would 'increase the maximum height by 8 feet' on residential blocks, 'from 240 feet to 248 feet on Block 7', and lists Block 5's existing maximum as 220 feet; Block 7 includes 7A, whose design review approval is about 237 ft. The committee-amended ordinance text (Leg Ver3 of BOS File 260770, Sept 28, 2026) shows a 'HIGHRISE TOWERS ON BLOCKS 5 AND 7' column with the range changed from 181'-240' to 191'-248'. The ordinance passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment number 209-26). The final text and the date it takes effect were not read, so 240 ft is the adopted limit this record still cites.

Unit count drift: 277 (press 2021) -> 325 (approval 2022) -> 319 (compliance reports' LBE appendix); the Planning Commission slides (July 2021) show '315' only on the 'Previous Phase 1' map inside Block 8 and '420' for Block 7 (7A with 7b) on the 'Current Phase 1' slide, so no slide gives a 7A-only count. Which figure a future permit will carry is unknown.

The SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says Associate Capital 'will move on to constructing a 300-unit market-rate apartment building and a waterfront park at the adjoining site'. The SF Standard (Aug 3, 2026) calls a 342-unit apartment complex Fifth Space's 'next building at the site', and DBI permit 202205194622 (151 Humboldt St, description '(block 8)', 342 residential units) is for Block 8, so Block 7A does not appear to be the next building.

Ground-floor childcare is assigned to Block 7 in the compliance reports. The April 25, 2023 Planning Director approval of the childcare amendment changed the Phasing Plan from two 6,000-sq-ft facilities in Phase 1 to 'two or three child care facilities' of at least 4,000 sq ft each, totaling at least 12,000 sq ft, with at least one in Phase 1; the Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary describes the existing control as 'Childcare Facilities may be provided on any Block' and proposes 'on any Block or within one mile of the Project'. Which facility goes on Block 7A is therefore not fixed by those documents; the design review approval shows about 6,270 sq ft of childcare in the building.
No cost, financing, general contractor or ground-lease information exists for Block 7A in any source found; the land is developer-owned (not Port), so no Port lease applies.

The 'Block 7A' / 'Block 7B' names are the sponsor's; the D4D treats Block 7 as one block with a single 240-ft highrise envelope. This record's map-shape note saying 7A/7B are 'informal press/developer labels' is consistent with the Planning documents, which nonetheless use 7A/7B as case names.

Block 7A rendering (Foster + Partners indicative views from the Design Review Approval packet) removed from the images shown here on 2026-09-29: the plan sheets are marked '(c) Foster + Partners 2020', which is not a licence to host them. The packet remains cited as a source (the Block 7A Design Review Approval); linked, not hosted.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the 2029 expected completion was removed. It rested only on October 2020 forecasts (the Phase 1 approval's 2020-2029 development schedule and SocketSite's October 9, 2020 block table), which its own basis note called stale; no current source gives Block 7A a completion year, and none is shown until one is sourced. The same pattern was removed from Humboldt Street Plaza on 2026-09-29.

Units on Block 7A: the design review approval (2022) gives 325 (unit mix 49 studios, 163 one-bed, 80 two-bed, 33 three-bed). Other stated values: 277 (press, March-June 2021); 319 (2021 and 2022 compliance reports, LBE section); approximately 325 (2021-2024 compliance reports, housing section). The July 2021 Planning Commission slides give no Block 7A-only count: their 'Current Phase 1' slide shows Block 7 (7A with 7b) at 420 units (their 315 is on the 'Previous Phase 1' map, inside Block 8).
